title: Farabbi2020: Motor-Imagery EEG dataset during robot-arm control
description: Motor-imagery EEG recorded from 12 healthy, BCI-naive participants who performed cued left- versus right-hand imagery to control a Baxter robot arm reaching toward objects. Each participant completed three sessions with first-person and third-person visual feedback conditions, giving 480 trials per subject. The dataset supports research on brain-computer interfaces and neurorehabilitation.
methods_description: EEG was recorded at 250 Hz with a 32-channel active Ag/AgCl LiveAmp system (Brain Products) in a 10-20 montage. Each session had four motor-imagery runs (first-person training and online, third-person training and online) plus a resting-state recording. Each run had 20 left-hand and 20 right-hand trials, and each trial consisted of a 2 s baseline followed by 4 s of imagery with visual feedback.
